customer_updates.name: Yogesh Sharma
customer_updates.text:
South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

While our experience, the food, and the service were great, what surprised me was a South Indian restaurant whose Sambar was so average. That being said, multiple visits to The Tanjore Tiffin Room are in my future.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

What amazed me most was how this world-famous network operates with such efficiency, accuracy, and coordination, largely without the use of advanced technology.

The dedication, discipline, and teamwork of the Dabbawalas are inspiring. Seeing this unique logistics system in action gave me a whole new appreciation for the people who keep Mumbai moving every day. A highly recommended experience for anyone visiting Mumbai and wanting to understand the city’s incredible work culture and spirit.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve tried so many things from Papa Pencho butter chicken, dal, chole bhature, kulche, dahi papdi chaat and not a single thing has ever disappointed me. Everything is consistently so good, which is honestly rare.

But if there’s one thing you have to try, it’s the Papa Pencho’s Tikka my absolute favourite. I literally beg you to order it. It’s that good.

This is one of those places I love with my whole heart. Always hits, always satisfies, and always something I keep going back to.

featured_reviews.name: Rivha Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imagine a dhaba in the middle of the city and that too in Bandra!! Well got an opportunity to visit “ Papa Pancho da Dhaba” with family. Was surprised on a Thursday night, it was crowded with people waiting to be seated, that is how popular the place is.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!
